archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (possession-first)
archetype.definition: A team that controls the puck and the shot count like a top-tier side, but whose finishing and goaltending have both run below league average, leaving it in the middle of the pack.

report.headline: Driving play like their old selves, finishing and saving like last year's Panthers
report.take:
Florida is two teams at once. In territory and shot volume it looks like the club that reached 16 playoff wins in both 2023-24 and 2024-25. Its 55% CF % ranks 4th, it puts 29.4 shots a game on net (6th), and it allows only 23.9 (also 6th), two shots above the league and three below it at either end. The results are much flatter. Goal Diff / GP is 0.06 (15th), goals scored a game rank 17th, and the 9-7-2 record has them sixth in a crowded Atlantic and 13th on the site.

The gap between process and results is mostly about percentages. The skaters are shooting 10.6% (24th, a point below the league's 11.6%), and the goalies together are stopping .886 (20th). At 5-on-5 that adds up to a PDO of 96.2, well under average. Pts vs Goal Diff is -0.3, so the record isn't hiding close-game luck in either direction. It is what the goals say, and the goals are being suppressed by bad bounces at both ends. One caution: xGF % is only 51.4% (15th). Florida wins the shot-attempt battle far more clearly than the chance-quality battle, so some of that volume is perimeter shooting, and that is part of why the shooting percentage is low.

The group grades of B-, B- and C fit that picture. Up front, Matthew Tkachuk (26 points, 9th of 126 wingers) and Brady Tkachuk (10 goals on a team-high 66 shots) drive the offense, with Reinhart and Verhaeghe supplying finish. Seth Jones is playing nearly 25 minutes and ranks 6th of 252 defensemen. The middle of the lineup is quiet, though. Bennett, Lundell and Luostarinen have good shot shares but few points. The third pair of Kulikov and Gudas is getting outshot badly. Neither Markstrom nor Schmid has given above-average goaltending: Markstrom's GSAx is -0.6 and Schmid's is 0.

The direction is the worry. November has gone 1-3 with four goals allowed a game, and the last five games allowed 3.6 a game, worse than the season rate. Last season also fell apart on defense and goaltending (defRank 28, team GSAx -8.8). If the save percentage settles near league average, the shot share should carry Florida into the playoff race. If it stays at .886, this is a bubble team that controls the puck.

strengths.title: Dominant shot share at both ends
strengths.body: Florida owns the puck at 5-on-5 and turns that into a big edge in shots on goal. They are top-six both in shots taken and shots prevented. That kind of structural edge usually holds over a season, and it is the main reason to expect better results ahead.

strengths.title: Elite penalty kill, solid power play
strengths.body: The PK is killing 85.7% of chances, 5th in the league and almost nine points above average. The power play is 10th at 23.5%. With 14 PP points for Matthew Tkachuk and 12 each for Brady Tkachuk and Jones, special teams are a net positive. The PK will likely drift down somewhat but should stay above average given how few shots this team allows.

strengths.title: A top tier of drivers
strengths.body: The two Tkachuks both rank in the top ten at their position, and Jones is a top-six defenseman on heavy minutes. That gives the B- groups a high ceiling at the top. The offense will run through them, and their shot shares (both above 56% xGF %) suggest the production is earned.

concerns.title: Goaltending hasn't stopped enough
concerns.body: Both goalies sit at .886, and the team's GSAx is 0, 19th in the league, against a league average around half a goal saved. The defense isn't the problem here: Florida allows few shots, yet still ranks only 10th in goals allowed a game. Given last season's -8.8 GSAx, this is a persistent issue as much as bad luck.

concerns.title: Volume without finish, and centers leaking
concerns.body: A 10.6% shooting rate (24th) and an xGF % far below the CF % point to plenty of low-danger attempts. Reinhart produces, but his on-ice xGF % is 0.44, and opposing centers score more than their averages suggest against Florida (rank 22nd). Centers take 43.3% of the points against this team, compared with 36.6% across the league. That points to a middle-of-the-ice coverage problem, not random variance.

concerns.title: Recent slide in goals against
concerns.body: Over the last five games Florida has allowed 3.6 a game, and November is 1-3. The losses came against Detroit, Washington and Boston. The underlying shot suppression hasn't obviously collapsed, so this looks more like goaltending and the soft third pair than a system failure. It still needs to stop soon.

trend.note: A winning October, including a three-game win streak, has given way to a 1-3 start to November in which goals against have jumped. The shot share has held up, so the dip is in results more than in play.

weekAhead.headline: Three bottom-third opponents, then Dallas on the back half of a back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games come against teams ranked in the bottom third on the site. Columbus (24th) scores less than almost anyone (offRank 29) and has D+ forwards, so Florida's shot suppression should hold. The Blue Jackets' goalies have been good, though (GSAx 4.6, 9th). Detroit (22nd) beat Florida 5-3 on Nov. 2, but it has the league's worst shooting percentage and a 69% PK (28th). That gives Florida's power play a real target in the home game. St. Louis (21st) gives up 28.5 shots a game and lets centers score above their averages (rank 26th), which suits a team that leans on Reinhart, Verhaeghe and Bennett.

Dallas is the outlier. The Stars are 8th on the site, 3rd in goals allowed, 1st on the PK, 3rd in GSAx, and they hold forwards far below their expected points. They also come on the second night of a road back-to-back after St. Louis. Anything less than five or six points from the first three games would be a missed chance. Dallas is a reasonable game to drop.

keyMatchups.title: Florida power play vs. Detroit's PK
keyMatchups.body: Detroit kills only 69% of penalties, 28th in the league, and Florida's power play converts 23.5%. With the Tkachuks and Jones carrying most of the PP production, this is where Florida can break the low-shooting spell. It also helps against a Detroit team that matches Florida in shot share.

keyMatchups.title: Florida centers vs. St. Louis
keyMatchups.body: The Blues let centers outscore their expected points by a wide margin (26th), and their blueline grades C-. Florida's centers draw a large share of its offense. The catch is St. Louis' B+ goaltending, the kind of goaltending that has frustrated this low-percentage shooting team.

keyMatchups.title: Shot volume vs. Dallas' wall
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows only 22.8 shots a game (3rd) and holds forwards far below their expected points (3rd). Its goaltending grades A. Florida's way of winning on volume runs straight into the league's best suppression, and it comes on the second half of a back-to-back.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Markstrom or Schmid can post a save percentage near league average against three weak offenses. If they can't against this schedule, the goaltending is a real problem, not a slump.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace is 41 wins and 91 points, which is roughly the bubble. The case for better is solid: top-six shot rates at both ends, an elite PK, and 5-on-5 percentages (PDO 96.2) that almost always drift back toward 100. If the shooting and save rates merely approach league average, Florida should finish in a 92-100 point range and contend for a top-three Atlantic spot. The two Tkachuks and Jones give it the top-end talent to support that.

The case for caution is just as specific. The chance share is only slightly above even, so the shooting may not recover fully. The goaltending carried a negative GSAx last season too, and the third pair and the defense against centers are real weak spots, not noise. The Atlantic is also crowded at the top. Expect gradual improvement rather than a surge, likely enough for a playoff spot but not enough to look like the Cup teams of 2023-24 and 2024-25.
swingFactors: Team save percentage moving toward league average
Shooting % recovering behind the shot volume
Defending opposing centers and the third pair

confidence.note: Eighteen games is enough for shot rates but not for the percentages.
